heroLead: Quaker City is a small village in Guernsey County, founded by Quaker settlers in the early 1800s, sitting inside the core of the Utica/Point Pleasant play where modern horizontal drilling has been active for over a decade.
intro: Guernsey County has been one of the more consistently drilled Utica counties since the mid-2010s, and Quaker City's position within that county puts local mineral owners in a reasonable spot to check for real, nearby production data rather than working off guesswork.

sections.heading: Historic settlement, modern drilling
paragraphs: Quaker City's founding families settled this land generations before anyone drilled a Utica well, which means mineral ownership here often traces through a long chain of family transfers. That history is worth confirming through a title search before you assume your ownership percentage matches what your family believes it to be.

sections.heading: Guernsey County's core position
paragraphs: This county sits within the thicker part of the Utica/Point Pleasant formation, and operators including Ascent Resources and Encino Energy have developed units throughout the area. A Quaker City-area tract's value depends on proximity to whichever units have actually been drilled nearby.

sections.heading: Checking records at the Guernsey County Recorder
paragraphs: The Guernsey County Recorder's office in Cambridge holds deed, lease, and unit records for Quaker City. Given the area's long settlement history, a thorough title search is worth the time before entering any sale discussion.

faqs.question: Is Quaker City in the Utica core?
faqs.answer: Yes, Guernsey County sits within the thicker part of the Utica/Point Pleasant formation, with steady development activity since the mid-2010s.

faqs.question: Why might my family's ownership percentage be unclear?
faqs.answer: Land settled generations ago and passed down through many family transfers can develop discrepancies between what a family believes it owns and what the official record shows. A title check resolves this.

faqs.question: Where do I check ownership records near Quaker City?
faqs.answer: The Guernsey County Recorder's office in Cambridge holds deed and lease records for the entire county.

faqs.question: Does Quaker City's founding history matter for a modern mineral sale?
faqs.answer: Not directly to value, but it does mean ownership often passed through many generations, so confirming your exact percentage through probate and deed records is an important step before negotiating.

faqs.question: How do I find out which specific unit my Quaker City parcel might be included in?
faqs.answer: Unit designations are recorded with the Guernsey County Recorder's office in Cambridge, and the Ohio Department of Natural Resources also maintains permit and unit records searchable by township and section.
